title: Kestrel and the Cipher
premise: Juniper Ravensworth, concierge at the grand but fading Hotel Meridian, has a gift for reading people — and a secret habit of solving the deaths no one else will question. When a confession letter arrives for a guest who died a week earlier, postmarked the day after his funeral, Juniper realizes the man was murdered and that the letter's cipher points to a ledger hidden in the hotel itself, one that could expose a smuggling ring protected by people he loves. As the killers close in on anyone who might decode it, Juniper must choose between protecting his found family of hotel staff — some of whom are implicated — and telling the truth that will destroy them. In the end he cracks the ledger, confronts the ringleader in the hotel's flooded basement, and chooses loyalty to truth: the guilty are arrested, the innocent band together, and Juniper finally accepts the Meridian's misfits as his real family.
about_author: C. M. Sterling spent a decade working night desks at grand old hotels, collecting the stories guests thought no one overheard. Now writing full-time from a coastal town much like the Meridian's, Sterling specializes in mysteries where the setting itself keeps secrets.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Checked Out Forever
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Juniper's POV. At the funeral of longtime guest Edmund Voss, Juniper notices details others miss: the widow's dry eyes, a lawyer's nervous glance, a stranger photographing the hotel. He recalls three past 'accidents' he quietly unraveled. Emotional beat: restless suspicion — the itch of a pattern beginning.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A confession letter addressed to Voss arrives, postmarked the day after the funeral — impossible timing. The letter is half cipher, half apology, mentioning 'the ledger under everyone's nose.' That night someone ransacks Voss's sealed room. Emotional beat: dread mixed with exhilaration; Juniper is pulled in.

chapters.title: The Meridian Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with a flashback to his first solved death. He maps the hotel's history and its tight-knit staff — housekeeper Marta, bartender Dez, night clerk Odile — realizing the 'ledger' may be embedded in the building itself. Police dismiss him again. Emotional beat: belonging; these people are his family, which raises the stakes.

chapters.title: A Cipher in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Decoding the letter, he finds references to room numbers, dates, and the lobby's stained-glass kestrel — the hotel's emblem. A second death occurs: the lawyer from the funeral falls from the fire escape. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; this is no accident.

chapters.title: What Marta Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Juniper and Marta. Marta admits she saw Voss meeting someone in the service corridors weeks before his death — but refuses to name them, terrified. Juniper realizes the killer is likely staff or a regular. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sting; trust begins to fracture.

chapters.title: The Kestrel's Eye
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the cipher, he finds a hidden compartment behind the stained glass containing part of the ledger — shipping manifests linking the hotel to a smuggling operation. Someone watches him from the mezzanine. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into isolation; knowing too much makes him a target.

chapters.title: Odile's Night Shift
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The night clerk's double life surfaces: she's been coerced into logging smugglers' deliveries for years. She nearly tells Juniper, then burns a page instead. Emotional beat: guilt and divided loyalty — she loves the hotel family she's deceiving.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Trapped overnight in the hotel during a storm, he deciphers the ledger's final key while the killer stalks the darkened corridors. Dez saves him from an attack, but Juniper spots mud on Dez's boots matching the service corridor. Emotional beat: terror and heartbreak — the suspect list now includes friends.

chapters.title: The Flooded Basement
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. Lured to the basement by a forged note 'from Marta,' he confronts the ringleader: Dez, who killed Voss and the lawyer to protect the operation that once saved him from ruin. Rising floodwater from the storm becomes their battleground; Juniper survives by out-thinking him, buying time until police arrive. Emotional beat: grief and clarity — love and truth collide.

chapters.title: Checkout Is at Noon
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, resolution. Dez is arrested; Odile confesses her coercion and is forgiven; Marta and the remaining staff rebuild trust. Juniper pins the decoded ledger's story to the hotel's history wall — truth displayed in plain sight. He turns down a detective's job offer, choosing the Meridian. Emotional beat: peace and belonging; found family, honestly kept.
